design_gotchas.title: Internal Back-to-Back Input Clamp Diodes Conduct Above ~0.6 V Differential Input
design_gotchas.detail: Per Section 5.1 Footnote (4), NE5532DR integrates anti-parallel input protection diodes across IN+ and IN-. Any differential input voltage exceeding ~0.6 V draws heavy current (abs max ±10 mA) unless externally limited by series resistors. Never drop NE5532DR into comparator, peak-detector, or slew-overdriven circuits designed for FET-input TL072IDR or OPA2134UA.

design_gotchas.title: Rev K (Dec 2025) Spec Changes: ±18 V Abs Max (Down from ±22 V) & 5 V/µs Slew Rate (Down from 9 V/µs)
design_gotchas.detail: TI Revision K updated NE5532DR absolute maximum supply from ±22 V (44 V) down to ±18 V (36 V), slew rate from 9 V/µs down to 5 V/µs, total ICC from 8 mA to 6 mA, and GBW from 10 MHz to 12 MHz (even though legacy prose in Sections 6.3 and 7.2 still mentions old figures). Audit legacy ±18 V–±20 V pro-audio rails and high-slew stages accordingly.

design_gotchas.title: High Bipolar Input Bias (200 nA Typ) & Current Noise (0.7 pA/√Hz) Degrade High-Z Sources
design_gotchas.detail: Although NE5532DR achieves an ultra-low 5 nV/√Hz voltage noise floor, its 200 nA typ (1000 nA max) bias current, 30 kΩ min input resistance, and 0.7 pA/√Hz (2.7 pA/√Hz at 30 Hz) current noise make it noisier and less accurate than FET-input OPA2134UA (5 pA) or TL072IDR (65 pA) when source impedances exceed ~10 kΩ.

design_gotchas.title: Commercial 0°C to 70°C Temp Grade, 10 V Min Supply & Non-Rail-to-Rail Headroom
design_gotchas.detail: NE5532DR is rated only 0°C to 70°C (use SA5532DR for -40°C to +85°C), requires at least ±5 V (10 V total) supply, and needs 2–3 V input/output headroom (±12 V min VICR on ±15 V). It cannot operate on 3.3 V or 5 V single-supply rails and dissipates 180 mW typ (480 mW max) quiescent power at ±15 V.

typical_use_cases: Pro-audio mixing consoles, microphone preamplifiers, and low-impedance (600 Ω) balanced line drivers
Active studio equalizers, RIAA phono stages, and low-noise DAC I/V analog filters on ±12 V/±15 V rails
AV receivers, broadcast video/audio distribution amplifiers, and low-source-impedance sensor buffers
Cost-effective 5 nV/√Hz bipolar alternative to OPA2134UA where low source impedance (<5 kΩ) permits
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments NE5532DR is a classic dual low-noise bipolar operational amplifier in an 8-pin SOIC (D) package specified for ±5 V to ±15 V (10 V to 30 V) operation over 0°C to 70°C. Featuring 5 nV/√Hz voltage noise at 1 kHz, 12 MHz GBWP, 100 dB CMRR, and 38 mA short-circuit drive capable of driving 600 Ω loads, it remains an audio benchmark on the standard dual SOIC-8 pinout. Designers must respect TI Rev K's updated ±18 V (36 V) absolute maximum supply and 5 V/µs slew rate, internal ±0.6 V differential input clamp diodes, 200 nA bipolar bias current, and 3 mA/ch (6 mA total) quiescent current.

audit_notes: Verified NE5532x SOIC-8 (D) Top View pinout on 300 DPI PNG page 2 (Figure 4-1 & Pin Functions table; Pin 1 labeled 1OUT in diagram and OUT1 in table).

Verified Rev K (Dec 2025) specifications on pages 3, 4, and 11 PNGs: ±18 V (36 V total) Abs Max, ±5 V to ±15 V (10 V–30 V) operating, 0°C–70°C NE5532 commercial temp grade, D RθJA = 97 °C/W, B1 = 12 MHz, SR = 5 V/µs, Vn = 5 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz.

Converted IIB = 200 nA -> 200000 pA and normalized total dual-channel ICC = 6 mA typ (16 mA max) -> iq_per_ch_typ_ua = 3000 µA/ch; verified NE5532DR Active Production status (vs obsolete NE5532D tube).
